title: Application Cannot Connect to RDS Database
symptom: Application crashes with 'OperationalError: (2003, "Can't connect to MySQL server on 'rds-db.xxx.rds.amazonaws.com' (110)")'.
initial_observations: Connection hangs and eventually times out (code 110).
environment: EC2 application instance connecting to AWS RDS MySQL/PostgreSQL in same VPC.

possible_causes.cause: RDS DB Security Group does not allow inbound traffic from EC2 instance Security Group
possible_causes.evidence_needed: RDS security group ingress rules do not contain EC2 SG ID or CIDR on port 3306/5432.
possible_causes.remediation: Add ingress rule to RDS Security Group allowing port 3306 (or 5432) with source set to EC2 Security Group ID.

possible_causes.cause: RDS placed in different VPC or subnet without routing/peering
possible_causes.evidence_needed: EC2 and RDS VPC IDs differ with no VPC peering connection active.
possible_causes.remediation: Move RDS to same VPC or configure VPC Peering / Transit Gateway.

investigation_steps.title: Test Network Socket Reachability
investigation_steps.explanation: Verify TCP layer connectivity to database port without running database driver.

investigation_steps.title: Inspect RDS Security Group Ingress Rules
investigation_steps.explanation: Identify attached security groups and inspect their rules.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Check security group ID and inbound rule for app port.

prevention: Reference security groups by ID across application and database tiers rather than hardcoded IP addresses.
